sanskrit: pratyāśvasto yadā rājā mohāt pratyāgataḥ punaḥ athājuhāva taṃ sūtaṃ rāmavṛttāntakāraṇāt
english: When the king had recovered and returned from his swoon, he summoned the charioteer again to learn of what had become of Rāma.

sanskrit: vṛddhaṃ paramasaṃtaptaṃ navagraham iva dvipam viniḥśvasantaṃ dhyāyantam asvastham iva kuñjaram
english: The charioteer was aged and utterly grief-stricken, sighing and brooding like an elephant newly captured, restless as a tormented bull-elephant.

sanskrit: rājā tu rajasā sūtaṃ dhvastāṅgaṃ samupasthitam aśrupūrṇamukhaṃ dīnam uvāca paramārtavat
english: The king, seeing the charioteer approach with his body covered in dust, his face full of tears, and looking wretched, spoke to him with the deepest anguish.

sanskrit: kva nu vatsyati dharmātmā vṛkṣamūlam upāśritaḥ so 'tyantasukhitaḥ sūta kim aśiṣyati rāghavaḥ bhūmipālātmajo bhūmau śete katham anāthavat
english: "Where will that righteous soul dwell, sheltered at the foot of a tree? That Rāghava who has always lived in the utmost comfort — what will he eat, O charioteer? How does this son of a king lie on the bare ground like one without a protector?"

sanskrit: yaṃ yāntam anuyānti sma padāti rathakuñjarāḥ sa vatsyati kathaṃ rāmo vijanaṃ vanam āśritaḥ
english: "He whom infantry, chariots, and elephants followed as he went — how will that Rāma now dwell in the desolate forest, bereft of all company?"

sanskrit: vyālair mṛgair ācaritaṃ kṛṣṇasarpaniṣevitam kathaṃ kumārau vaidehyā sārdhaṃ vanam upasthitau
english: "How have the two princes, together with Vaidehī, entered a forest roamed by wild beasts and deer and frequented by black serpents?"

sanskrit: sukumāryā tapasvinyā saha sītayā rājaputrau kathaṃ pādair avaruhya rathād gatau
english: "How did the two princes descend from the chariot on foot together with the delicate, suffering Sītā?"

sanskrit: siddhārthaḥ khalu sūta tvaṃ yena dṛṣṭau mamātmajau vanāntaṃ praviśantau tāv aśvināv iva mandaram
english: "Fortunate indeed are you, O charioteer, for you have seen my two sons entering the forest's edge, like the twin Aśvins entering Mandara."

sanskrit: kim uvāca vaco rāmaḥ kim uvāca ca lakṣmaṇaḥ sumantra vanam āsādya kim uvāca ca maithilī āsitaṃ śayitaṃ bhuktaṃ sūta rāmasya kīrtaya
english: "What words did Rāma speak? What did Lakṣmaṇa say? And what did Maithilī say upon reaching the forest, O Sumantra? Tell me how Rāma sat, how he slept, how he ate."

sanskrit: iti sūto narendreṇa coditaḥ sajjamānayā uvāca vācā rājānaṃ sabāṣpaparirabdhayā
english: Thus urged by the lord of men, the charioteer spoke to the king in a voice choked and suffused with tears.

sanskrit: abravīn māṃ mahārāja dharmam evānupālayan añjaliṃ rāghavaḥ kṛtvā śirasābhipraṇamya ca
english: "Rāghava, ever upholding righteousness, folded his hands and bowed his head and addressed me thus, O great king."

sanskrit: sūta madvacanāt tasya tātasya viditātmanaḥ śirasā vandanīyasya vandyau pādau mahātmanaḥ
english: "'O charioteer, on my behalf bow your head at the feet of that great-souled father of mine who knows the true Self and is worthy of reverence, and salute those feet with your head.'"

sanskrit: sarvam antaḥpuraṃ vācyaṃ sūta mad vacanāt tvayā ārogyam aviśeṣeṇa yathārhaṃ cābhivādanam
english: "'Convey on my behalf greetings of health and respectful salutations without distinction to all the inner apartments, O charioteer.'"

sanskrit: mātā ca mama kausalyā kuśalaṃ cābhivādanam devi devasya pādau ca devavat paripālaya
english: "'And to my mother Kausalyā, convey my greeting of well-being and reverential salutation. O queen, honor the feet of the king as though they were the feet of a god.'"

sanskrit: bharataḥ kuśalaṃ vācyo vācyo madvacanena ca sarvāsv eva yathānyāyaṃ vṛttiṃ vartasva mātṛṣu
english: "'Bharata is to be greeted with my words of well-being, and tell him: conduct yourself properly toward all the mothers in accordance with what is right.'"

sanskrit: vaktavyaś ca mahābāhur ikṣvākukulanandanaḥ pitaraṃ yauvarājyastho rājyastham anupālaya
english: "'That mighty-armed delight of the Ikṣvāku lineage is also to be told: holding the rank of crown prince, protect and serve the father who holds the sovereignty of the kingdom.'"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ māṃ mahārāja bruvann eva mahāyaśāḥ rāmo rājīvatāmrākṣo bhṛśam aśrūṇy avartayat
english: "Even as he spoke these words to me, O great king, that Rāma of great renown and lotus-red eyes shed abundant tears."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇas tu susaṃkruddho niḥśvasan vākyam abravīt kenāyam aparādhena rājaputro vivāsitaḥ
english: "But Lakṣmaṇa, greatly enraged, sighing deeply, spoke: 'For what offence has this prince been banished?'"

sanskrit: yadi pravrājito rāmo lobhakāraṇakāritam varadānanimittaṃ vā sarvathā duṣkṛtam kṛtam rāmasya tu parityāge na hetum upalakṣaye
english: "'If Rāma has been exiled — whether because of greed, or on account of the granting of a boon — it is in every way a wicked deed. Yet in the abandonment of Rāma I can perceive no reason whatsoever.'"

sanskrit: asamīkṣya samārabdhaṃ viruddhaṃ buddhilāghavāt janayiṣyati saṃkrośaṃ rāghavasya vivāsanam
english: "'This act, undertaken impulsively without proper deliberation, contrary to righteousness and born of shallow judgment, will generate universal lamentation — the exile of Rāghava.'"

sanskrit: ahaṃ tāvan mahārāje pitṛtvaṃ nopalakṣaye bhrātā bhartā ca bandhuś ca pitā ca mama rāghavaḥ
english: "'As for me, I no longer recognize the great king in the role of father. Rāghava alone is my brother, my master, my kinsman, and my father.'"

sanskrit: sarvalokapriyaṃ tyaktvā sarvalokahite ratam sarvaloko 'nurajyeta kathaṃ tvānena karmaṇā
english: "'Having abandoned one who is dear to all the world and devoted to the good of all the world — how can all the world rejoice in you through this deed?'"

sanskrit: jānakī tu mahārāja niḥśvasantī tapasvinī bhūtopahatacitteva viṣṭhitā vṛṣmṛtā sthitā
english: "And Jānakī, O great king — the suffering one, sighing deeply — stood there like one whose mind has been seized by a spirit, like a cow whose calf has died."

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapūrvavyasanā rājaputrī yaśasvinī tena duḥkhena rudatī naiva māṃ kiṃ cid abravīt
english: "That illustrious princess, who had never before experienced such calamity, wept from that grief and said not a single word to me."

sanskrit: udvīkṣamāṇā bhartāraṃ mukhena pariśuṣyatā mumoca sahasā bāṣpaṃ māṃ prayāntam udīkṣya sā
english: "With her face grown dry and gazing upward at her husband, she suddenly released a flood of tears upon seeing me depart."

sanskrit: tathaiva rāmo 'śrumukhaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ sthito 'bhaval lakṣmaṇabāhupālitaḥ tathaiva sītā rudatī tapasvinī nirīkṣate rājarathaṃ tathaiva mām
english: "Just so, Rāma stood with tears on his face and hands folded in salutation, supported by the arm of Lakṣmaṇa. Just so, the suffering Sītā, weeping, watched the royal chariot — and so she watched me."

sanskrit: mama tv aśvā nivṛttasya na prāvartanta vartmani uṣṇam aśru vimuñcanto rāme saṃprasthite vanam
english: "When I turned back, my horses would not move forward on the road, shedding warm tears as Rāma set out for the forest."

sanskrit: ubhābhyāṃ rājaputrābhyām atha kṛtvāham ajñalim prasthito ratham āsthāya tad duḥkham api dhārayan
english: "After saluting both princes with folded hands, I mounted the chariot and departed, bearing that grief within me."

sanskrit: guheva sārdhaṃ tatraiva sthito 'smi divasān bahūn āśayā yadi māṃ rāmaḥ punaḥ śabdāpayed iti
english: "Together with Guha I remained there many days, hoping that Rāma might call me back again."

sanskrit: viṣaye te mahārāja rāmavyasanakarśitāḥ api vṛkṣāḥ parimlānaḥ sapuṣpāṅkurakorakāḥ
english: "In your domain, O great king, worn by the affliction of Rāma's exile, even the trees have withered, along with their flowers, sprouts, and buds."

sanskrit: na ca sarpanti sattvāni vyālā na prasaranti ca rāmaśokābhibhūtaṃ tan niṣkūjam abhavad vanam
english: "Creatures no longer creep about, nor do beasts of prey roam forth. Overwhelmed by grief for Rāma, that forest has fallen silent."

sanskrit: līnapuṣkarapatrāś ca narendra kaluṣodakāḥ saṃtaptapadmāḥ padminyo līnamīnavihaṃgamāḥ
english: "O lord of men, the lotus ponds have their leaves and petals drooping, their waters turbid, their lotuses scorched; the fish and water-birds in the lotus pools have retreated and hidden."

sanskrit: jalajāni ca puṣpāṇi mālyāni sthalajāni ca nādya bhānty alpagandhīni phalāni ca yathā puram
english: "Water-born flowers and garlands, and those that grow on land, no longer shine as before — they are faint of fragrance — nor do the fruits appear as they once did."

sanskrit: praviśantam ayodhyāṃ māṃ na kaś cid abhinandati narā rāmam apaśyanto niḥśvasanti muhur muhuḥ
english: "As I re-entered Ayodhyā no one welcomed me. The people, not seeing Rāma, sigh again and again."

sanskrit: harmyair vimānaiḥ prāsādair avekṣya ratham āgatam hāhākārakṛtā nāryo rāmādarśanakarśitāḥ
english: "From their mansions, terraces, and palaces, the women — haggard from not seeing Rāma — observed the returning chariot and raised a cry of 'Alas! Alas!'"

sanskrit: āyatair vimalair netrair aśruvegapariplutaiḥ anyonyam abhivīkṣante vyaktam ārtatarāḥ striyaḥ
english: "With long, clear eyes flooded with a torrent of tears, the women glanced at one another, clearly more distressed than ever."

sanskrit: nāmitrāṇāṃ na mitrāṇām udāsīnajanasya ca aham ārtatayā kaṃ cid viśeṣaṃ nopalakṣaye
english: "Among enemies, friends, and those who are indifferent — in their anguish I perceive no distinction whatsoever."

sanskrit: aprahṛṣṭamanuṣyā ca dīnanāgaturaṃgamā ārtasvaraparimlānā viniḥśvasitaniḥsvanā
english: "Its people without joy, its horses and elephants wretched and troubled, its voice pained and faded, resounding with sighs —"

sanskrit: nirānandā mahārāja rāmapravrājanātulā kausalyā putra hīneva ayodhyā pratibhāti mā
english: "— joyless, O great king, made incomparable in grief by the banishment of Rāma, Ayodhyā appears to me like Kausalyā bereft of her son."

sanskrit: sūtasya vacanaṃ śrutvā vācā paramadīnayā bāṣpopahatayā rājā taṃ sūtam idam abravīt
english: Having heard the charioteer's words, the king, in a voice utterly desolate and overcome with tears, spoke these words to that charioteer.

sanskrit: kaikeyyā viniyuktena pāpābhijanabhāvayā mayā na mantrakuśalair vṛddhaiḥ saha samarthitam
english: "Instigated by Kaikeyī of wicked character, I did not deliberate this with the skilled elder counselors."

sanskrit: na suhṛdbhir na cāmātyair mantrayitvā na naigamaiḥ mayāyam arthaḥ saṃmohāt strīhetoḥ sahasā kṛtaḥ
english: "Without consulting friends, ministers, or citizens — out of delusion, on account of a woman, I acted in haste in this matter."

sanskrit: bhavitavyatayā nūnam idaṃ vā vyasanaṃ mahat kulasyāsya vināśāya prāptaṃ sūta yadṛcchayā
english: "This great calamity has surely come by the force of fate, or by chance, for the destruction of this dynasty, O charioteer."

sanskrit: sūta yady asti te kiṃ cin mayāpi sukṛtaṃ kṛtam tvaṃ prāpayāśu māṃ rāmaṃ prāṇāḥ saṃtvarayanti mām
english: "O charioteer, if any merit has been accumulated by me as well, bring me swiftly to Rāma — my very life-breaths are urging me."

sanskrit: yad yad yāpi mamaivājñā nivartayatu rāghavam na śakṣyāmi vinā rāma muhūrtam api jīvitum
english: "Whatever command of mine can recall Rāghava — let it be used. Without Rāma I cannot live even for a moment."

sanskrit: atha vāpi mahābāhur gato dūraṃ bhaviṣyati mām eva ratham āropya śīghraṃ rāmāya darśaya
english: "Or if that mighty-armed one has gone too far away, then mount me on the chariot and take me swiftly to show me to Rāma."

sanskrit: vṛttadaṃṣṭro maheṣvāsaḥ kvāsau lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ yadi jīvāmi sādhv enaṃ paśyeyaṃ saha sītayā
english: "Where is he — that great bowman with well-formed teeth, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa? If I should live, let me see him together with Sītā."

sanskrit: lohitākṣaṃ mahābāhum āmuktamaṇikuṇḍalam rāmaṃ yadi na paśyāmi gamiṣyāmi yamakṣayam
english: "If I do not see Rāma — the red-eyed, mighty-armed one adorned with jewelled earrings — I shall journey to the realm of Yama."

sanskrit: ato nu kiṃ duḥkhataraṃ yo 'ham ikṣvākunandanam imām avasthām āpanno neha paśyāmi rāghavam
english: "What can be more painful than this — that I, having fallen into this plight, do not see here the joy of the Ikṣvākus, Rāghava?"

sanskrit: hā rāma rāmānuja hā hā vaidehi tapasvinī na māṃ jānīta duḥkhena mriyamāṇam anāthavat dustaro jīvatā devi mayāyaṃ śokasāgaraḥ
english: "Alas, Rāma! Alas, younger brother of Rāma! Alas, O suffering Vaidehī! You do not know that I am dying of grief like one without a protector. O queen, this ocean of sorrow is impossible to cross alive."

sanskrit: aśobhanaṃ yo 'ham ihādya rāghavaṃ didṛkṣamāṇo na labhe salakṣmaṇam itīva rājā vilapan mahāyaśāḥ papāta tūrṇaṃ śayane sa mūrchitaḥ
english: "Inauspicious is my fate — I who seek Rāghava here today yet cannot find him together with Lakṣmaṇa!" — lamenting thus, that king of great renown fell suddenly on his bed, overcome by unconsciousness.

sanskrit: iti vilapati pārthive pranaṣṭe karuṇataraṃ dviguṇaṃ ca rāmahetoḥ vacanam anuniśamya tasya devī bhayam agamat punar eva rāmamātā
english: As the king lamented and fell senseless, and hearing his words — more pitiable still, and redoubled with grief for Rāma — Rāma's mother, the queen, was seized once again by fear.

sanskrit: tato bhūtopasṛṣṭeva vepamānā punaḥ punaḥ dharaṇyāṃ gatasattveva kausalyā sūtam abravīt
english: Then Kausalyā, trembling again and again as though possessed by a spirit, like one whose life had ebbed away to the ground, spoke to the charioteer.

sanskrit: naya māṃ yatra kākutsthaḥ sītā yatra ca lakṣmaṇaḥ tān vinā kṣaṇam apy atra jīvituṃ notsahe hy aham
english: "Take me to where Kākutstha is, where Sītā is, where Lakṣmaṇa is. Without them I have no courage to live here even for a moment."

sanskrit: nivartaya rathaṃ śīghraṃ daṇḍakān naya mām api atha tān nānugacchāmi gamiṣyāmi yamakṣayam
english: "Turn the chariot around quickly and take me too to the Daṇḍaka forest. If I do not follow them, I shall go to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: bāṣpavegaupahatayā sa vācā sajjamānayā idam āśvāsayan devīṃ sūtaḥ prāñjalir abravīt
english: Struck by a flood of tears and his voice faltering, the charioteer, with hands folded in salutation, spoke these words to console the queen.

sanskrit: tyaja śokaṃ ca mohaṃ ca saṃbhramaṃ duḥkhajaṃ tathā vyavadhūya ca saṃtāpaṃ vane vatsyati rāghavaḥ
english: "Abandon grief, delusion, and the distress born of anguish. Shaking off affliction, Rāghava shall dwell well in the forest."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaś cāpi rāmasya pādau paricaran vane ārādhayati dharmajñaḥ paralokaṃ jitendriyaḥ
english: "And Lakṣmaṇa too, who knows righteousness and has conquered his senses, serves Rāma's feet in the forest and thereby wins merit for the world beyond."

sanskrit: vijane 'pi vane sītā vāsaṃ prāpya gṛheṣv iva visrambhaṃ labhate 'bhītā rāme saṃnyasta mānasā
english: "Even in the lonely forest, Sītā, having found her dwelling, is at ease as in a house — fearless, with her mind surrendered to Rāma."

sanskrit: nāsyā dainyaṃ kṛtaṃ kiṃ cit susūkṣmam api lakṣaye uciteva pravāsānāṃ vaidehī pratibhāti mā
english: "I perceive not the slightest sign of dejection in her, even the most subtle. Vaidehī appears to me as one accustomed to travel abroad."

sanskrit: nagaropavanaṃ gatvā yathā sma ramate purā tathaiva ramate sītā nirjaneṣu vaneṣv api
english: "Just as she used to delight in going to the city's pleasure groves of old, so too does Sītā delight even in the solitary forests."

sanskrit: bāleva ramate sītā bālacandranibhānanā rāmā rāme hy adīnātmā vijane 'pi vane satī
english: "Like a child she takes delight, this Sītā of moon-like face — truly, even dwelling in a solitary forest, her spirit is undaunted when she is with Rāma."

sanskrit: tadgataṃ hṛdayaṃ hy asyās tad adhīnaṃ ca jīvitam ayodhyāpi bhavet tasyā rāma hīnā tathā vanam
english: "For her heart is fixed on him alone and her life depends on him alone — even Ayodhyā would be as the forest to her if it were empty of Rāma."

sanskrit: pathi pṛcchati vaidehī grāmāṃś ca nagarāṇi ca gatiṃ dṛṣṭvā nadīnāṃ ca pādapān vividhān api
english: "Along the road, Vaidehī asks about the villages and towns, and upon seeing the courses of rivers and the various trees, she questions about them too."

sanskrit: adhvanā vāta vegena saṃbhrameṇātapena ca na hi gacchati vaidehyāś candrāṃśusadṛśī prabhā
english: "Neither the road, nor the wind's force, nor commotion, nor the heat of the sun dims the radiance of Vaidehī — a radiance resembling the rays of the moon."

sanskrit: sadṛśaṃ śatapatrasya pūrṇacandropamaprabham vadanaṃ tadvadānyāyā vaidehyā na vikampate
english: "The face of that Vaidehī, speaking so sweetly, resembling the lotus in form and the full moon in its light, does not waver or lose its lustre."

sanskrit: alaktarasaraktābhāv alaktarasavarjitau adyāpi caraṇau tasyāḥ padmakośasamaprabhau
english: "Her two feet, even now as before, are as brilliant as lotus buds — red-hued as the dye of lac-resin even without application of lac."

sanskrit: nūpurodghuṣṭaheleva khelaṃ gacchati bhāminī idānīm api vaidehī tadrāgā nyastabhūṣaṇā
english: "Even now, that spirited Vaidehī walks with a playful gait as if to the sound of her anklets, still radiant with that natural glow though her ornaments have been set aside."

sanskrit: gajaṃ vā vīkṣya siṃhaṃ vā vyāghraṃ vā vanam āśritā nāhārayati saṃtrāsaṃ bāhū rāmasya saṃśritā
english: "Sheltered in the forest, even upon seeing an elephant, or a lion, or a tiger, she takes no fright — for she takes refuge in the arms of Rāma."

sanskrit: na śocyās te na cātmā te śocyo nāpi janādhipaḥ idaṃ hi caritaṃ loke pratiṣṭhāsyati śāśvatam
english: "They are not to be mourned, nor are you to mourn for yourself, nor even for the lord of the people — for this conduct will be established in the world as eternally glorious."

sanskrit: vidhūya śokaṃ parihṛṣṭamānasā maharṣiyāte pathi suvyavasthitāḥ vane ratā vanyaphalāśanāḥ pituḥ śubhāṃ pratijñāṃ paripālayanti te
english: "Shaking off sorrow, with joyful hearts, well-settled on the path trodden by the great sages, delighting in the forest, subsisting on forest fruits — they are upholding your father's noble promise."

sanskrit: tathāpi sūtena suyuktavādinā nivāryamāṇā sutaśokakarśitā na caiva devī virarāma kūjitāt priyeti putreti ca rāghaveti ca
english: Yet even so, though restrained by the charioteer speaking such well-reasoned words, the queen, worn thin by grief for her son, did not cease her cries of "My dear!" and "My son!" and "O Rāghava!"
